scheme_name: World Bank MSME Development Programme India
overview: The World Bank MSME Development Programme India is part of the World Bank Group's Country Partnership Framework (CPF) for India FY2026-2031, which aims to support India's aspiration to become an upper-middle-income economy and achieve Viksit Bharat by 2047. The programme focuses on fostering rural prosperity and resilience, driving urban transformation, empowering people through better skills and health, and building resilient infrastructure and boosting energy security, with a cross-cutting emphasis on private sector-led job creation and MSME growth and innovation.
objectives: Foster rural prosperity and resilience by supporting secure and better-paying jobs in rural areas, diversifying rural incomes beyond agriculture, strengthening value chains and market access, and improving water management
Drive urban transformation by supporting investments in infrastructure, housing, and services, and promoting innovative financing and integrated planning for sustainable, livable cities

Empower people through better skills and health by supporting government plans to upgrade skilling institutions, mainstreaming a skills approach to education interventions, and digital skilling and technology-enabled learning

Build resilient infrastructure and boost energy security by scaling up infrastructure through upgraded business models that can crowd in private sector capabilities and capital, prioritizing transport, logistics, digital connectivity, water supply, wastewater treatment and reuse, water storage and flood management, waste management and circular economy, and scaling up solar and wind energy, promoting e-mobility and frontier technologies
Unlock private investment in job-rich sectors and foster more conducive conditions for MSME growth and innovation
Promote entrepreneurship, particularly for youth and women, through cross-cutting engagements
eligibility: The evidence does not specify explicit eligibility criteria for the World Bank MSME Development Programme India. Eligibility is inferred to align with the CPF's focus on MSMEs, youth, and women, particularly in rural and urban areas benefiting from CPF interventions.
benefits: Benefits include access to improved agricultural/food market linkages or trade (AgriConnect) for 150 million people, improved access to finance for small producers especially women, support for high-potential agribusiness firms, modernization and climate-proofing of agriculture including irrigation, strengthening integrated water resources management, and enabling resilient infrastructure and energy security through private sector mobilization and global innovation leverage.
financial_support: The CPF aims to provide US$8–10 billion in financing annually from the World Bank Group to help unlock another US$20 billion annually from markets by the end of the CPF period. By mobilizing private capital (Budget Plus) and leveraging global innovation (Finance Plus), the CPF aims to deliver tangible results including millions of new jobs especially for youth and women, resilient prosperous rural communities, more livable cities, better skilled and healthier workforce, better more resilient infrastructure, expanded access to clean energy, and an enabling environment for MSMEs.
application_process: The evidence does not describe a numbered step-by-step application procedure for the World Bank MSME Development Programme India. Implementation occurs through the CPF's engagement with government, private sector, and development actors.
deadlines: The CPF period is FY2026-2031; specific application deadlines are not detailed in the evidence.
caveats: The CPF is a strategic framework; specific MSME development activities are implemented through various projects and trust funds under the framework
Financial targets are indicative and subject to annual approvals and market conditions
